I've been farming these 13.1 mu for 30 years now — me and my wife, just the two of us. I only finished middle school, but I've sat through enough village trainings and talked to enough dealers and neighbors to know what works on this land. I don't need any book to tell me what my own eyes have seen.

The winter wheat went in last October. I used an improved variety, same type as Old Wang on the east end of the village — if his yields are steady, mine will be too. Before planting, I put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, that's one and a half bags. Come spring when it greens up, I topdress with another 40 jin of urea per mu. The dealer told me that works out to about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I know that's not cheap — fertilizer prices have gone up — but I'd rather put on a bit too much than risk a thin harvest. A bad year means I dig into my savings; wasting some fertilizer is just money I spent, not a disaster. I irrigate three times: once at green-up in March, once at jointing in April, and once during grain filling in May. I spray twice for pests and disease. Before last fall's planting I ran the rotary tiller. I'm expecting around 550 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For the summer maize, right after wheat harvest in early June, I hire the machine to plant direct — no-tillage. In double-cropping, three days saved is everything, and with only two of us I can't afford to be turning soil by hand. I plant hybrid seed, about 2 jin per mu. At sowing I put down 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, and at the big flare stage I topdress 35 jin of urea. That's about 17 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing if it's dry, and once at tasseling in late July or early August. Two pesticide sprays — one for weeds early, one for corn borers later. I expect about 650 kg per mu.

I thought about cutting fertilizer back to save money, but then I looked at my whole budget. If I spend less on fertilizer and the yield drops, I lose more than I saved. So I kept fertilizer the same as last year and decided not to hire extra labor for hand-weeding — me and my wife will do that ourselves. That's the tradeoff. Last year my neighbor Zhang used similar rates and did fine, so I'm sticking with what I know.
